title: Responder Succession and Knowledge Guardian Playbook
author: Priya Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines a repeatable program for responder succession, knowledge preservation, and rotation debriefs. The goal is to reduce single-player risk across critical responder roles, preserve tribal knowledge in an auditable way, and make on-call transitions predictable and low-friction. This doc complements runbooks and incident policies by focusing on personnel continuity rather than purely technical remediation steps.

Scope:
- Applies to all primary responders for Redwood public-facing inference services (API gateway, routing fabric, runtime pools, and cache layer).
- Target audience: on-call engineers, incident commanders, team leads, and SRE apprentices.
- Exclusions: purely business/CS communications owned by GTM; platform recruitment/hiring processes.

Goals and success metrics:
- Mean time to knowledge transfer (MTKT): < 7 days from shadowing to primary take.
- Runbook coverage: >95% of runbook steps validated during shadow rotations each quarter.
- Post-rotation confidence: >= 4/5 average on debrief survey.
- Reduction in knowledge-related escalations: 40% fewer owner-unknown escalations within 6 months.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Knowledge Guardian (KG): A semi-formal role assigned per service team for a 3-month term. Responsibilities: maintain canonical runbooks, curate incident postmortems, own the rotation checklist, and host weekly transfer office hours.
- Primary Responder: Person currently on the rotation who handles first response for P0/P1 events.
- Shadow/Apprentice: Trainee assigned to observe and assist for at least one full rotation window and two live incidents before being cleared.
- Incident Commander (IC): Leads incident coordination (same as standard incident process).

Succession & rotation process (step-by-step):
1. Pre-rotation handoff (7 days before change):
   - Outgoing primary creates a "Handoff Snapshot" (see template below) and uploads to team-runbook.
   - KG runs a 60-minute knowledge transfer session: architecture overview, common throttles, debugging routes, and recent flake causes.
   - Confirm that the incoming primary has read and acknowledged three recent P0 postmortems.
2. Shadow week (first 7 days):
   - Incoming primary shadows outgoing on calls, monitors alerts, and follows remediation steps without sole ownership.
   - KG verifies runbook step execution during a synthetic or low-risk failover drill.
3. Primary transition (day 8):
   - Outgoing signs the checklist and becomes fallback for 72 hours.
   - Runbook version is stamped and the KG updates the changelog.
4. Post-transition validation (days 9–21):
   - Incoming completes a short quiz (tooling auto-generated) covering SLA thresholds, throttles, and the top 5 triage commands.
   - KG runs a 30-minute debrief at day 21; update runbook gaps.

Shadowing & apprenticeship program:
- Minimum requirements to be cleared as primary: shadow one full rotation, assist in two incidents (evidence logged), pass the KG quiz, and receive at least one positive debrief from the outgoing primary.
- Apprenticeship cohort: pairs of apprentices per team meet weekly with the KG for problem-focused labs (e.g., KV cache eviction debugging, OOM trace triage).

Handoff Snapshot template (to be attached to every rotation):
- Service: API-router-v2
- Primary outgoing: name, pager, slack
- Primary incoming: name, pager, slack
- Runbook version: v2026-07-12
- Active experiments/rollouts: model-routing canary on region eu-west-1 (ID: canary-8421)
- Known noisy neighbors: tenant-42 high-saturation pattern (mitigation: limit qps to 120/m per tenant)
- Open action items: list with owners and ETA

Post-rotation debrief template (30 minutes):
1) Quick wins & friction points (5 mins each)
2) Runbook gaps discovered (10 mins)
3) Knowledge handoff items to add (5 mins)
4) Training follow-ups and dates (5 mins)
- Deliverable: KG updates runbook and opens tracking tickets for any procedural gaps.

Game day integration:
- Game days are mandatory for KG and incoming primaries at least once per quarter.
- Scenario focus areas (rotate quarterly): KV cache pressure, prefix cache invalidation regression, multi-region routing fallback, quantization-induced latency spikes.
- Game day outcomes must exercise the full succession process: shadowing, signage, debrief, and runbook update.

Status page & customer comms templates (concise, editable snippets):
- TL;DR (public-facing):
  "We are experiencing degraded inference throughput for customers in eu-west-1 due to a model routing regression. Our team is actively mitigating and we expect restoration within 45 minutes. Status: Degraded — Partial Outage."
- Technical update (engineering channels/internal):
  "Root cause hypothesis: new routing policy pushed to router v2 causing incorrect shard selection under specific seq-length distributions. Temporary mitigation: rollback router policy to v2.3, route 10% traffic to fallback pool. Next step: run targeted perf job and promote patch if stable. IC: @name; KG: @name."
- Customer status follow-up (30 minutes):
  "Service restored for affected regions. We rolled back an experiment and are running verification traffic. A post-incident summary will be published in our customer portal within 48 hours."

Runbook governance and pruning cadence:
- KG owns the service runbook but must coordinate quarterly with product & runtime to validate SLO numbers and rehearsal steps.
- Pruning policy: remove steps with no execution evidence in >12 months after a KG sign-off; archive as 'historical' with link to why it was removed.
- Versioning: major version bump for structural changes, patch version for text fixes. Each version requires a short changelog entry (1-3 lines).

Evidence, logging and change audit:
- All handoff snapshots and debrief notes must be stored in the team-runbook directory with a standard filename: handoff-<service>-YYYYMMDD-<outgoing>-<incoming>.md
- Incident evidence related to knowledge handoffs (screenshares, permissions escalations) must be referenced in postmortem artifacts.

Escalation paths when knowledge gaps cause delay:
1. Immediate escalation to KG (P0) with a TL;DR and an ask (e.g., temporary owner, step 3 executed).
2. If KG is unavailable, escalate to team lead for temporary assignment.
3. For cross-functional escalation (multiple teams affected), IC calls for cross-team knowledge-synthesis meeting and assigns a temporary knowledge owner.

Debrief survey (post-rotation):
- 5 questions, 1–5 Likert scale: confidence in runbook; clarity of handoff; sufficiency of shadowing; access to tooling; suggestions. KG must reach out if average confidence < 3.5.

Operational templates (examples to paste into runbook):
- Quick triage command list (copy into runbook):
  1) authz: curl -sS https://internal-api/status | jq .tokens_in_flight
  2) routing: rctl routes list --service api-router-v2 --filter canary
  3) kv-cache: redis-cli -h cache-eu.z query 'INFO memory'
- Runbook stamping CLI (example):
  # stamp-runbook versioning and changelog
  stamp-runbook --service api-router-v2 --version v2026-09-01 --author "Priya Patel" --notes "Added shadow checklist"

Appendix: Example handoff snapshot (markdown)
---
Service: api-router-v2
Outgoing: Priya Patel (pager: +1-555-0102)
Incoming: Daniel Kim (pager: +1-555-0144)
Runbook: v2026-07-12
Active rollouts: router-policy-canary-8421 (10% traffic)
Known issues: tenant-42 qps spikes; mitigation: manual rate-limit to 120/m
Open items: ticket #TIX-3442 to increase burst-capacity; owner: infra-team; ETA: 2026-09-30
---

Implementation checklist for teams (owner: KG):
- [ ] Define KG for service and publish office hours
- [ ] Audit runbook against most recent P0 in last 90 days
- [ ] Schedule shadow cohort and game day within next 60 days
- [ ] Create handoff snapshot before each rotation
- [ ] Automate the KG quiz and evidence collection in our runbook tool
